verses.mystical_translation: When the inward work is done, the people remove the idols that once stood between them and YHWH; each returns to the place he is called to keep holy.
Order placed around sacrifice gathers voices of thanksgiving, so the city may be a tent where praise is constant.
A ruler’s portion becomes a sacrament of time—daily and festival offerings bind polity to covenant.
Support for teachers is a strengthening of the law’s living voice among the people.
The people’s hands bring first fruits—earth’s gifts and labors offered deeply, a visible thanksgiving.
Animals and holy gifts are gathered into ordered heaps—visibility of communal devotion and provision.
What begins in spring reaches fullness by festival time—order measured by months marks providence.
Leaders behold the people’s abundance and their mouths become blessing, joining the community’s hymn.
A ruler questions the custodians of the sacred store, seeking to align abundance to holy use.
When the altar receives the people's gifts, need is satisfied and surplus becomes a sign that YHWH’s favor rests upon the community.
Rooms are made within the house so the sacred offerings may dwell under care and order.
Faithful hands set the heaps; named stewards stand as sign and anchor of communal trust.
A chain of named servants distributes care—service multiplied through accountable hands.
Gate and offering meet: the porter toward the east mediates what the people give and what the sanctuary keeps most holy.
Order reaches every household: named men serve so even the least among kin receive their portion.
Even the youngest who serve are counted—service and provision measured from the doorway of three years onward.
Lineage and age shape responsibility; the community entrusts service by generation and maturity.
Household boundaries extend the sanctuary’s care—whole families set apart within the community’s service.
Even those who dwell at the city edge are named and provided for—the priestly household extended into fields and towns.
The king’s reforms read as faith in action—good, right, and true become the measure of rule.
Wholehearted seeking brings success; devotion to law and to YHWH bears communal fruit.

contemplative_note: Abundance of offerings follows reform: generosity, order, and redistribution sustain both cult and community.
safety_note: Contains unsanitized religiously-motivated destruction and institutional coercion; preserved as in source.
